sites.label: Decoder
sites.blurb: How it runs, one forward pass
sites.title: Transformer Decoder Explained: how one forward pass works
sites.name: Transformer Decoder Explained
sites.claim: The TypeScript transformer in your browser is checked against PyTorch, operation by operation, to within 1e-5, and the animations' frames against a float64 PyTorch run of the same seeded weights.

sites.label: Training
sites.blurb: How it learns, from one step to many GPUs
sites.title: Transformer Training Explained: how the same decoder is trained
sites.name: Transformer Training Explained
sites.claim: A NumPy reference of the trainer matches PyTorch autograd (to 1e-12) and torch.optim, and the trainer in your browser matches that reference step for step.

sites.label: Kernels
sites.blurb: How a GPU executes the maths
sites.title: GPU Kernels Explained: how a GPU executes the maths
sites.name: GPU Kernels Explained
sites.claim: The GPU model is checked against the CUDA Programming Guide's worked examples (coalescing, bank conflicts, occupancy), and its TypeScript port reproduces the Python reference exactly.

sites.label: Systolic
sites.title: Systolic Arrays Explained: inside a matrix engine
sites.name: Systolic Arrays Explained
sites.claim: The cycle-accurate model's output-stationary frames match a SystemVerilog array simulated in Verilator 5.020 on every accumulator after every clock edge: 613 values, 0 mismatches.

sites.label: Accelerators
sites.title: AI Accelerators Explained: the families of AI silicon
sites.name: AI Accelerators Explained
sites.claim: Every specification carries its source and the date it was read, vendor claims are never used as inputs, and the model is checked against published capacity, throughput and latency figures.

sites.label: Racks
sites.blurb: GPUs, networks, power, cooling at scale
sites.title: AI Racks Explained: GPUs, networks, power and cooling at scale
sites.name: AI Racks Explained
sites.claim: Every hardware figure carries its source and the date it was read, and the model is checked against published rack, switch and fabric totals that it does not take as inputs.

sites.label: Serving
sites.title: LLM Inference Explained: how real systems generate text
sites.name: LLM Inference Explained
sites.claim: The serving simulator in chapters 11–14 is Disaggregated_Inference_Sim's own engine, copied byte for byte from a pinned commit, and CI requires every request's timestamps to match its Python original; the tiny model's cached logits are bit-identical to full recomputation.

sites.label: Architectures
sites.title: LLM Architectures Explained: how model designs differ
sites.name: LLM Architectures Explained
sites.claim: Every value links to its source, and the modelled parameter count of 80 of the 86 open models whose published weights can be counted is within 0.5% of those weights at a pinned commit.

sites.label: Numerics
sites.title: Numerics Explained: number formats and quantisation
sites.name: Numerics Explained
sites.claim: Every code of every format up to 16 bits is checked against numpy and ml_dtypes, and the TypeScript port in your browser reproduces the Python reference exactly.

sites.label: Trade-offs
sites.title: Inference Trade-offs Explained: which lever helps which metric
sites.name: Inference Trade-offs Explained
sites.claim: For every one of the 350 sweep points, the simulator's JavaScript engine (the one the what-if runs in your browser) reproduces the recorded TTFT, TPOT and ITL percentiles of the Python run exactly.

sites.label: Harnesses
sites.blurb: The loop between a model and the world
sites.title: Agent Harnesses Explained: the loop between a model and the world
sites.name: Agent Harnesses Explained
sites.claim: Agent_Loop_Sim's Python reference and the TypeScript port in your browser produce the same events, token for token and float for float, and three recorded runs of a small open-weights model are replayed token for token.

sites.label: Protocols
sites.title: Agent Protocols Explained: MCP, transports, auth and A2A
sites.name: Agent Protocols Explained
sites.claim: The engine sends the same 160 messages as the official MCP Python SDK (mcp 2.3.0) over 18 recorded sessions, and the same 56 as the official A2A SDK (a2a-sdk 1.2.2), compared as JSON.

sites.label: Context
sites.title: Agent Context Explained: retrieval, memory and context engineering
sites.name: Agent Context Explained
sites.claim: Every retrieval number is measured on 200 SQuAD questions with real MiniLM embeddings and recorded reranker scores, and the TypeScript engine in your browser reproduces the Python reference exactly, with no tolerance.

sites.label: Orchestration
sites.title: Agent Orchestration Explained: graphs, multi-agent patterns and durability
sites.name: Agent Orchestration Explained
sites.claim: Each of 39 sessions also runs in real LangGraph 1.2.14, and after every one of 71 operations its whole checkpoint history equals the engine's.

sites.label: Evals
sites.title: Agent Evals Explained: measuring agents
sites.name: Agent Evals Explained
sites.claim: The estimators are tested against scipy and statsmodels on a synthetic benchmark whose truth is known, and the TypeScript engine in your browser reproduces every Python fixture bit for bit.

sites.label: Security
sites.title: Agent Security Explained: threats and defences
sites.name: Agent Security Explained
sites.claim: The trifecta check agrees with an exhaustive search on all 256 tool subsets, and the TypeScript engine in your browser reproduces the Python reference's fixtures exactly.

sites.label: Compute in transit
sites.blurb: Computing on gradients in the network
sites.title: Compute in Transit: an investigation of computing on gradients in the network
sites.name: Compute in Transit
sites.claim: Every vendored file is its source byte for byte at a pinned commit, the TypeScript port reproduces every cell of the simulation's results.md that it can, character for character, and the loss curves are recomputed from the run logs.

sites.label: HW Design-Space Agent
sites.name: HW Design-Space Agent
sites.claim: Every number comes from a recorded run of the agent, vendored byte for byte with its hashes; the TypeScript ports of its golden model and cost model match the Python reference exactly, and CI fails if anything drifts.
